authority: Observed findings and dispositions; no item is omitted merely because it was repaired during the audit.

findings.finding: Failed Windows test cleanup retries stranded four PX-owned workspaces and consumed about 23.6 GiB.
findings.disposition: Bounded read-only-aware cleanup retries, exact-root validation, regression coverage, and governed reconciliation reclaimed all four workspaces with zero failures.

findings.finding: A Linux VS Code CLI launched under WSL prompts interactively and blocks noninteractive VSIX installation.
findings.disposition: The owned Linux host sets VS Code's documented DONT_PROMPT_WSL_INSTALL override only for the isolated child.

findings.finding: The Linux certification profile assumed the Windows `python` launcher even though Ubuntu exposes `python3`.
findings.disposition: The isolated workspace and host test now select python on Windows and python3 on non-Windows platforms.

findings.finding: The installed-host listener test assumed a desktop trash service and Windows shell commands.
findings.disposition: The disposable Linux profile disables trash and uses platform-native terminal/task commands while retaining VS Code file-operation listeners.

findings.finding: A crash after a signed Studio event write but before head replacement left a valid trailing event that ordinary reconciliation could not consume.
findings.disposition: Explicitly approved recovery accepts exactly one authenticated linked trailing event and rejects tampering, illegal transitions, missing ancestry, or multiple-event divergence.

findings.finding: The first formal fault campaign correctly failed because the generated provider-route index was stale.
findings.disposition: The route index was rebuilt from current source; the same two-lane/eight-dimension campaign then passed.

findings.finding: The Windows installed test host briefly reported extension-host unresponsiveness while built-in GitHub authentication performed account probes.
findings.disposition: PX activation was independently measured at 4.544 ms with zero activation subprocesses, discovery, or project writes; the external built-in work is not attributed to PX and did not invalidate the host receipt.

findings.finding: NVIDIA hardware is visible but the current Python environment has no compatible CUDA execution backend.
findings.disposition: PX selects zero GPU workers and deterministic CPU fallback. Compatibility, exact-workload benchmark, correctness, VRAM, OOM and fallback logic remain gated and tested; no speedup is claimed.
